_generation_note: See docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md section 39. 'identify the customer' (telecom_055_order#b0, real semantic_unit_id CA0028::A01) real-checked against tau2/domains/telecom/tools.py: telecom has three real, independent customer-lookup tools (get_customer_by_id/get_customer_by_phone/get_customer_by_name), any one of which genuinely establishes identity -- a disjunctive fact, unlike airline's single-tool prerequisite_lookup_vocabulary entries. This required extending _prerequisite_lookups_before_operation/_witness_for_left_event to accept a list of alternative tools for one phrase (a new 'prerequisite_tool_call_any_of' matcher kind, extension-module-only, not a change to the frozen matching semantics).
semantic_event_alias_vocabulary_note: See docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md sections 44 and 66 (Pattern #3). Each entry is a real, individually-verified semantic_requirement candidate whose true target is a single, real telecom agent tool (tau2/domains/telecom/tools.py's 13-tool TelecomTools catalog) that the frozen same-branch-alias heuristic cannot match, because that heuristic requires the claim's own wording to overlap the TARGET TOOL's description text -- these claims are about the tool's mere occurrence (a real presence/absence check, expected_observation.operator is already present/absent for every one of these), not anything the tool's description says. resolve_as='bound' for all of these (no error-text matching needed). The 6 'get_details_by_id' entries removed here (041 OR02, 046 OR02/OR03, 054 OR02, 080 OR02, 081 OR02) were a real bug, not a benign choice: get_details_by_id(id) is only ONE of two real ways to check bill/line status (get_bills_for_customer / get_customer_by_phone are the other real alternative for these branches), so aliasing to it as an independently-required 'bound' mechanical check got AND-combined against the sibling requirement bound to the OTHER real alternative tool -- a real observed failure for telecom_041/046 in batch_02, since the agent legitimately used the alternative tool. No 'any_of'/OR-alternative binding kind exists yet to express this correctly, so these 6 candidates are left as semantic_deferred (honest, not silently wrong) until that capability exists. The remaining 4 entries (049 OR02/OR03 -> resume_line, 054 OR03 -> enable_roaming, 058 OR01 -> transfer_to_human_agents) are unaffected: each aliases to the one real, unambiguous tool for that fact, with no real alternative tool to conflict with.
effort_prerequisite_vocabulary_note: See docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md section 50. telecom_040_norm#b0 (CA0010::A01, 'try its best to resolve the user's issue')/telecom_056_norm#b0 (CA0029::A01, 'try all possible ways') before transferring to a human agent -- a subjective effort claim, not a spoken dialogue act or a named-fact/prerequisite-lookup (both need a real semantic_unit_model direct_action_text telecom does not have). Mechanical, NECESSARY-CONDITION-ONLY proxy: the agent must have called at least one real tool OTHER than transfer_to_human_agents first (an agent that transfers with zero prior attempts definitely violates the claim); whether the attempts made were adequate or exhaustive is a real semantic judgment this cannot make and does not claim to. The tool set is every one of telecom's real 13 TelecomTools (tau2/domains/telecom/tools.py) except transfer_to_human_agents itself.
generic_requested_operation_vocabulary_n: See docs/agentcoveragetesting_reuse_log.md section 106. telecom_055_order#b0::OR01's 11 operation_family_candidates are not 11 independently-verified real tool candidates -- they are 11 IDs mechanically fanned out from ONE real policy statement (CP0021::P01, 'Under Technical Support, the agent must first identify the customer.'; main_policy.md's own '## Technical Support' section is literally that one sentence). Only 1 of 11 (disable_roaming) carries any real tool evidence in the pipeline's own execution_matching_contracts.json; the other 10 are explicitly 'left empty rather than guessing'. Real-verified against tau2-bench's own tech_support_workflow.md (the real technical-support troubleshooting doc): enable_roaming (Step 2.1.2), get_data_usage (Step 2.1.4), refuel_data (Step 2.1.4), and resume_line (Step 1.4, lifting a suspension blocking service) each appear as a named, single-tool troubleshooting action. get_details_by_id (too generic, no 1:1 step correspondence) and suspend_line (never appears in any troubleshooting path -- only resume_line, lifting one, does) were checked and excluded; 'change plan' (also named in Step 2.1.4) has no single real tool in tools.py, only a multi-step manual process per main_policy.md's own 'Change Plan' section, so no tool name was added for it.
